transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Hello um thank you for calling S-Net Mobile Support my name is Sonia how can I help you today

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Sonia my name is Giancarlo and I'm in a complete mess with my mobile number transfer from Vodafone that started yesterday morning

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I gave S-Net my PAC code on Tuesday and yesterday at about two o'clock my outgoing calls and data started working on my new S-Net eSIM on my Pixel eight

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: But anybody who rings my number or sends me a banking text message still gets routed to my old Vodafone SIM so I have a completely split service right now

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Oh gosh I am so sorry you've been stuck in limbo like that since yesterday I completely understand how stressful it is when people and bank texts can't reach you properly

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay um let me pull up the MNP port file right now can you give me the mobile phone number you are transferring over and your date of birth please

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah sure the mobile number is zero seven seven eight nine four four two one zero six and my date of birth is the nineteenth of August nineteen eighty-four

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me just type that mobile number in zero seven seven eight nine four four two one zero six and nineteenth of August eighty-four

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait I think my microphone clipped for a second it's zero seven seven eight nine four four two one zero six yeah you got it right

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Lovely um and just to open the billing screen on my system what are the last four digits of the bank account used for your direct debit

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The last four digits of the bank account are nine zero three two

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great I'm into your mobile account profile now and I'm opening the Mobile Number Portability console to look at yesterday's PAC transfer batch

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Because honestly I run a catering supply van and all morning my commercial kitchen clients have been ringing me and going straight to the old Vodafone voicemail unless I carry two phones around

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I really do feel for you having to juggle two phones in your van while trying to run your business I would be pulling my hair out too

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah and when I rang Vodafone earlier they told me they already released the number at eleven o'clock yesterday morning so they said S-Net has to finish the last step

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes I can see the exact Vodafone release timestamp from eleven fifteen yesterday morning right here in the port gateway log so you definitely don't need to chase Vodafone again

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh thank goodness because I really didn't want to get bounced back and forth between two networks all afternoon

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No I am taking full responsibility for sorting this out right here on the call with you today you won't be passed anywhere else

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So what actually happened to my number on your system then if the outgoing calls work on my Pixel eight eSIM

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well looking at the MNP sequence here step one and step two completed which activated your outbound calling line identity and mobile data on our S-Net core

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right that matches what I'm seeing when I call out to my suppliers my proper number shows up on their screens

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yeah and then step three is the central numbering database broadcast where our gateway tells every other UK network to route incoming calls and SMS messages to S-Net instead of Vodafone

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And let me guess step three got stuck somewhere in the queue yesterday afternoon

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Spot on um the step three broadcast packet threw a timeout error at sixteen forty-two yesterday when the central Syniverse routing switch was busy and it just sat in a stalled retry state

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is wild so for the last twenty hours half the country's phone networks still think my number belongs to the old Vodafone SIM card

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Pretty much yes because until that final central routing table acknowledgement completes inbound voice and SMS traffic from external networks keeps hitting the donor network switch

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And that's also why my bank one-time passcode texts for my catering wholesaler login were landing on the old handset instead of my Pixel eight

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly right short-code banking SMS aggregators read from the exact same central UK numbering routing table as incoming voice calls

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay so is there a way for you to manually push that stuck broadcast update through right now or does it take another twenty-four hours

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can manually clear the stalled flag and force an immediate high-priority MNP broadcast push to the central UK numbering gateway from my console right now

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh brilliant if you can do that live while we're talking that would save my afternoon deliveries

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm going to build the manual port completion command on the switch now um can I place you on a brief hold while I push the MNP broadcast file through to the central numbering gateway

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah of course go ahead I'll wait on the line

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding um I've pushed that port broadcast update through now and the central UK numbering database just returned a green completed status code

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait really it came back green already

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes the donor routing table on Vodafone's gateway has now officially terminated the old route and all five major UK mobile and landline switches have acknowledged S-Net as the host network

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The signal bars on the old phone sitting on my passenger seat literally just dropped to 'No Service' right in front of my eyes

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Aha when the old Vodafone SIM drops to No Service that is the clearest sign that the donor line has finally closed down completely

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Should I restart my Pixel eight so the S-Net eSIM picks up the new inbound routing cleanly

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wait are you speaking to me right now on the Pixel eight or on another phone

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm calling you from my partner's phone right now so my Pixel eight is sitting right here in my hand ready to test

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Oh that's ideal then um toggle Aeroplane Mode on for five seconds and back off on your Pixel eight so the eSIM re-registers fresh on our IMS voice core

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay tapping Aeroplane Mode on now... waiting five seconds... and turning Aeroplane Mode off again

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can see your Pixel eight eSIM re-attaching to the 5G cell tower on my network monitor right now and VoLTE voice registration shows active

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah full 5G bars are back at the top of the screen on the Pixel eight

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Lovely let me place a live test call from my outbound support desk line to your zero seven seven eight nine number right now so we can verify incoming calls hit your Pixel eight

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Go for it I'm looking at the Pixel eight screen now

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's dialling out from our external test trunk now... did that test call come through now

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes it's ringing right here on my Pixel eight on the S-Net eSIM! Let me decline it so I don't cut you off on this phone

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Awesome I saw the ring alert hit your Pixel eight eSIM directly and I also just triggered an automated network confirmation SMS to test your inbound text routing

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ping! The text message just popped up on the Pixel eight notification bar straight away

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And let me also check your voicemail box provisioning on the S-Net side because sometimes a stalled port leaves voicemail forwarding disabled

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh good thinking I definitely need voicemail working when I'm driving between restaurant drop-offs

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yeah I can see conditional call forwarding on busy and no-answer was still pointing to a blank placeholder so I've just bound it to your S-Net voicemail box now

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me also quickly click 'Send Code' on my catering wholesaler banking app to see if the short-code text comes through to the Pixel eight now

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes please test that banking one-time passcode while I stay on the line with you that way we know external SMS aggregators have updated too

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Clicked it... and boom the six-digit banking code just arrived on the Pixel eight in less than two seconds

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Less than two seconds you can't ask for better than that and your PAC port status on the account is now permanently marked as Fully Completed

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can I take the old Vodafone SIM out of the spare phone and bin it now then

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes that old Vodafone SIM is completely deactivated now so you only need to carry your Pixel eight from here on out

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And will my monthly bill just show my normal unlimited business plan from today without any weird charges from the stuck port

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your billing cycle started cleanly yesterday on the unlimited plan at twenty-two pounds a month and I've actually added a five-pound goodwill credit to your next invoice for the twenty-hour port delay

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh that's really decent of you Sonia I didn't even expect a credit I just wanted my clients to be able to ring me

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's the least I can do after you had to drive around with two phones in your catering van all morning

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait I literally just got a call waiting notification on the Pixel eight from one of my restaurant chefs in Soho so regular incoming calls are definitely working

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Haha there is the ultimate live proof right there! Let me check if there are any open tasks left on your MNP order before I let you take your chef's call

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Take a look I can ring him back in sixty seconds

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Everything on the MNP port order and the 5G provisioning profile is green and closed off with zero errors

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Brilliant outgoing calls work incoming calls ring on the Pixel eight and my banking texts are coming through instantaneously

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So are you happy that your mobile number transfer and incoming service are completely resolved now

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah completely sorted Sonia you saved my day honestly

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wait let me also pop the five-pound credit confirmation text onto your phone so you have a record of that too

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Got that text just now as well

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fantastic stuff I'll let you get back to your deliveries and your Soho chef

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks a million Sonia have a great afternoon

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome thank you for choosing S-Net and have a safe drive this afternoon bye now
